title: The Only Two Real Skills in the World

content:
there are only two real skills in the world (being locally talented isn't enough)

Today I realised there are only two real skills in the world. If you don't have them, no matter how talented you are, you will always be replaceable and your impact on the world and your compensation will always be limited. One is organizing or mobilising people, the second is strategically allocating your resources, including your own time and brainpower. Let me explain. Regardless of what your actual job is, the amount of impact and value you create is gated on these two things. Because there's only so much anyone can do as an individual. Most of where you end up is due to the momentum of those around you, which means you have to be good at choosing the right games to play. And getting those around you to help you get what you want by creating alignment between your personal interest and the often contradictory things that they want. And if you are good at these things, you will succeed to some extent anyway, whether you're working for somebody else or yourself. This was a huge breakthrough for me because a lot of the things in my life that felt like very different problems I was ruminating on all tie down to this. Because I realized no matter where I worked or what I did for a living or how much money I made, I would always feel dissatisfied with myself until I was good at creating impact. There are some people who are very locally talented, as in they have creativity and hustle and intelligence, and if you give them a task they will accomplish it very well. If this is you, you can love what you do and make a great living, but you'll always be a pawn on the chessboard, always replaceable, never one of the big dogs. I think I'm one of these people by the way. I don't think I have long term vision or strategy. So far I have lived my life reactively. But I know people who from a young age thought very intentionally about how the larger structures around them would move. They make such strategic choices and function so effectively within organisations that by their mid-20s they've gotten further than most people get in their whole lives. For obvious reasons, I am fascinated by these people. I've been trying to figure out what they read, what they pay attention to, what things they work on getting better at. I want to know where they look and what they try to see. Most of all, I want to know a good place to start training this skill. Maybe it's playing chess, maybe it's investing, maybe it's just being proactive and pitching projects to people and trying to make something take off. If you know someone to be like this or you have any recommendations, let me.
